claims.text: High-temperature toughness and plastic strain in fusion plasma-facing structural materials are governed primarily by dynamic recrystallization and precipitate dissolution.
Dynamic recrystallization refines the grain structure.
Dynamic recrystallization promotes dissolution of brittle precipitates.
Grain refinement and precipitate dissolution lower stress concentrations and ease dislocation motion.
A conventionally processed fusion-grade tungsten alloy or high-strength steel has relatively coarse grains and intact precipitate distributions.
High-temperature annealing can trigger dynamic recrystallization and associated precipitate dissolution without introducing additional phases or detrimental defects.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1200°C are representative of fusion-relevant plasma-facing operating conditions for the proposed materials.
At fusion-relevant temperatures, thermally activated dynamic recrystallization refines grain size and facilitates dislocation glide and climb.
Dissolution of embrittling precipitates minimizes stress concentrations at grain boundaries.
The combined grain refinement and precipitate dissolution enhance plastic deformation capacity and toughness.
Annealed samples will have statistically significantly greater strain-to-failure than untreated samples.
Annealed samples will have statistically significantly greater fracture toughness or impact-energy absorption than untreated samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit reduced grain size and diminished or altered precipitate distributions.
The mechanism should apply only where dynamic recrystallization occurs without deleterious phase transitions and may fail outside 800–1200°C or in materials with secondary-phase instabilities.

contradictions.description: The intervention attributes dynamic recrystallization to a pre-test annealing treatment, whereas the mechanism describes it as occurring at fusion-operation temperatures during deformation. The hypothesis does not resolve whether the intended mediator is annealing-induced static recrystallization or deformation-coupled dynamic recrystallization.

The intervention is required to induce grain refinement and precipitate dissolution, but the falsification rule treats failure to induce either mediator as falsification of the causal hypothesis. Such a result could instead mean that the intervention failed to implement the hypothesized microstructural change.
